The maximum recorded total length of Otolithoides biauritus, based on extensive trawl surveys across its coastal range, has been documented at 160 centimeters [Li = 160 centimeters]. This exceptionally large size places the species among the largest sciaenids in the Indo-West Pacific, a status reflected in its adult body mass, which reaches approximately 27,700 grams [Wwi = approximately 27,700 grams]. Such substantial body dimensions are supported by a robust, elongate form that allows the species to exploit a wide spectrum of benthic and demersal prey, from small crustaceans to forage fishes. Field studies indicate that individuals experience a prolonged juvenile phase before transitioning to a reproductive state; the shift to sexual maturity, marked by the initial appearance of vitellogenic oocytes in gravid females, is associated with a total length of 93 centimeters [Lp = 93 centimeters]. At this size, the corresponding wet weight is roughly 5,400 grams [Wwp = roughly 5,400 grams], a body mass that reflects the culmination of several years of sustained somatic growth in the relatively warm waters of the Bay of Bengal and the South China Sea.

Reproductive output in Otolithoides biauritus has been assessed through histological examination of ripe ovaries, revealing that females produce an extraordinarily large number of eggs over the course of a spawning season. At a stable ambient water temperature of 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C], a single mature female releases, on average, approximately 1,941,400 eggs per spawning event [N_R_i = approximately 1,941,400 eggs per spawning event], and typically only one spawning event occurs per year [F_R_i = one spawning event occurs per year]. This reproductive strategy, characterized by a very high fecundity per unit time, is consistent with an r-selected life-history trajectory observed in many large-bodied, low-latitude teleosts. The daily output, derived by combining per-clutch fecundity with spawning frequency, is substantial, although it is rarely measured directly in the field; rather, it is inferred from the product of the two independently measured sub-components. The maximum lifetime reproductive rate at this thermal regime remains one of the highest recorded among sciaenids.

The earliest stages of life for Otolithoides biauritus begin with a small, pelagic egg; the diameter of a fully hydrated, fertilized ovum has been measured at 0.79 millimeters, a dimension typical of sciaenid eggs that undergo a brief incubation period in the water column. Upon completion of yolk absorption and the onset of first exogenous feeding, the newly hatched prolarvae are remarkably diminutive, with a wet weight at the conclusion of the yolk-sac stage of just 0.00026 grams [Wwb = 0.00026 grams]. This extremely low initial mass, equivalent to roughly a quarter of a milligram, underscores the profound growth trajectory that must be achieved over the subsequent months and years. The hatchlings are entirely dependent on their endogenous yolk reserves during the first few days post-eclosion, after which the mouth gape opens and they begin to capture small planktonic copepods. The period from fertilization to the completion of yolk-sac resorption lasts approximately three to four days at the prevailing temperatures of 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C], a rapid endogenous phase that is characteristic of tropical marine fish larvae.

Longevity estimates for Otolithoides biauritus have been derived from otolith microstructure analysis, which provides a reliable archive of annual growth increments. The maximum lifespan documented for this species is approximately 10,950 days [am = approximately 10,950 days], a considerable age that reflects a slow-paced life history once maturi at a temperature of 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C]ty is attained. This lifespan estimate was recorded from individuals inhabiting stable thermal environments where the average annual water temperature remains close to 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C]; such warm conditions are typically associated with accelerated metabolic rates, yet the species manages to attain a remarkably long life. The combination of a very large ultimate body size, a late onset of maturation at 93 centimeters total length, and a long reproductive window suggests that Otolithoides biauritus occupies a distinctive demographic niche within the sciaenid community. Comparative studies with congeneric species, such as Otolithoides pama, indicate that the longevity of Otolithoides biauritus is among the greatest in the genus, likely driven by reduced natural mortality rates experienced by adults in deeper offshore habitats.

The energetic investment in reproduction by Otolithoides biauritus is intimately tied to its body size at the onset of sexual maturation. Females that have achieved the length at puberty of 93 centimeters [Lp = 93 centimeters] possess a corresponding body mass of roughly 5,400 grams [Wwp = roughly 5,400 grams], a size at which they begin vitellogenesis and become capable of spawning. This mass represents a substantial accumulation of somatic tissue relative to the minute initial mass of 0.00026 grams [Wwb = 0.00026 grams] at the yolk-sac stage. A comparison of these two life-stage weights reveals a multiplicative increase of over twenty million-fold, one of the largest documented growth ratios among marine fishes. The eventual attainment of the ultimate wet weight of 27,700 grams [Wwi = 27,700 grams] in the largest adults, corresponding to the ultimate total length of 160 centimeters [Li = 160 centimeters], further emphasizes the species' capacity for extreme size. The underlying anatomical and physiological mechanisms enabling such growth include a highly efficient digestive system and a diet rich in high-energy prey items, which together support the energetic demands of both somatic maintenance and the production of millions of eggs over a lifespan of approximately 10,950 days [am = approximately 10,950 days] at a temperature of 28.4 °C [T = 28.4 °C].
